title: Box model and responsive layout
runtime: Modern evergreen browser. HTML, CSS, and JavaScript fragments can be tried in a small local page or the browser DevTools described in the lesson.

objectives.text: Explain content, padding, border, margin, and box-sizing.
Build a flexible layout with normal flow, Flexbox, or Grid.
Make content adapt without targeting named devices.

learningFlow: Apply it to a fresh page

diagnostic.question: With content-box, does width include padding and border?
diagnostic.answer: No. width sets the content box; padding and border add to the rendered size.

sections.title: Every rendered element has boxes
sections.body: The content box holds content. Padding adds space inside the border. The border surrounds padding and content. Margin creates space outside the border. Background usually paints through the padding but not the margin. DevTools can show every layer.

sections.title: Use predictable sizing
sections.body: With content-box, declared width and height describe the content box. With border-box, they include content, padding, and border. Many projects apply box-sizing: border-box to all elements and pseudo-elements because component sizes become easier to reason about.

sections.title: Normal flow is the starting layout
sections.body: Block elements normally stack; inline content flows inside lines. Use Flexbox for one main row or column and Grid for two-dimensional tracks. Avoid absolute positioning for ordinary page structure because removed elements no longer reserve normal-flow space.

sections.title: Prefer flexible constraints
sections.body: Use available space with percentages, flex sizing, grid minmax, and max-width. A readable container can be width: min(100% - 2rem, 70rem). Images commonly need max-width: 100% and height: auto so they shrink inside their container.

sections.title: Add a breakpoint when content needs it
sections.body: Start with a simple narrow layout. Add a min-width media query when the content has enough room for another arrangement. Choose the breakpoint by resizing until the design needs to change, not by memorizing a phone model. Respect zoom, long text, and user font settings.

sections.title: Components need container awareness
sections.body: A React component can appear in many widths. Avoid assuming the whole viewport describes its space. Flexible internal layout and, later, container queries can make a component adapt where it is placed.

examples.title: Predictable cards
examples.explanation: The card never exceeds its container, and its declared width includes padding and border.
examples.tryThis: Remove border-box and calculate the extra horizontal size.

examples.title: A grid that adapts
examples.explanation: The grid creates as many useful columns as fit and falls back to one column without a device-specific breakpoint.
examples.tryThis: Increase the minimum card size and observe when columns wrap.

practice.prompt: An image causes horizontal scrolling on a narrow screen. Give a CSS fix and explain it.
hints: Let the image shrink without changing its aspect ratio.
acceptanceCriteria: Explain the evidence or rule behind the answer.

solution.code: img { max-width: 100%; height: auto; } prevents the image from exceeding its container while preserving its ratio. Also inspect fixed widths on its ancestors.

practice.prompt: Choose Flexbox or Grid for a toolbar and for a gallery. Explain each choice.
hints: Think in one dimension versus rows and columns.
acceptanceCriteria: Explain the evidence or rule behind the answer.
Complete the attempt before opening the solution.

solution.explanation: Use Flexbox for a toolbar arranged mainly along one row with aligned controls. Use Grid for a gallery where both columns and rows matter. Either can work, but the chosen model should match the layout problem.

interviewQuestions.question: Explain the CSS box model and box-sizing.
interviewQuestions.answer: An element has content, padding, border, and margin areas. content-box excludes padding and border from declared size; border-box includes them.
interviewQuestions.followUp: Does margin become part of width?

interviewQuestions.question: When would you choose Flexbox over Grid?
interviewQuestions.answer: Flexbox is useful for arranging items mainly in one dimension. Grid is useful when rows and columns form the layout. Content and behavior matter more than a rigid rule.

interviewQuestions.question: What does mobile-first responsive design mean?
interviewQuestions.answer: Write the simple narrow layout first, then add enhancements when more space is available. Breakpoints should follow the content, not named devices.
interviewQuestions.followUp: How do you test beyond changing window width?

commonMistakes.symptom: A 300px box is wider than expected
commonMistakes.cause: content-box adds padding and border outside the declared width.
commonMistakes.fix: Use border-box or include the extra size in your calculation.

commonMistakes.cause: A fixed-width child, long content, or media exceeds its container.
commonMistakes.fix: Use DevTools to find the overflowing box; add flexible sizing or wrapping at the cause.

commonMistakes.symptom: A layout uses absolute positioning for every card
commonMistakes.cause: The cards are removed from normal flow and overlap as content changes.
commonMistakes.fix: Use Grid or Flexbox for layout; reserve absolute positioning for intentional overlays.
